web_evidence.title: Summer Sisters: Read the Prologue – Judy Blume on the Web
web_evidence.note: The author's authorized prologue sustains external narration of Victoria and Caitlin, including Victoria's private thoughts, in third person.

web_evidence.title: Summer Sisters Character Analysis | SuperSummary
web_evidence.note: Explicitly describes an omniscient third-person narrator centered mostly on Vix that regularly cuts to other characters' perspectives.

web_evidence.title: Judy Blume Writing Styles in Summer Sisters
web_evidence.note: Its point-of-view analysis explicitly identifies Vix's majority narration as third person and describes the interspersed material as shifts of third-person viewpoint.

web_evidence.title: Summer Sisters (1998) by Judy Blume – Cannonball Read
web_evidence.note: The review describes the secondary-character glimpses and reproduces an interior example in which Abby's private thoughts are rendered as she, corroborating shifting third-person focalization.

web_evidence.title: Tome Raider: Summer Sisters | The Harvard Crimson
web_evidence.note: This review ambiguously calls the interspersed viewpoints 'first person perspectives,' but describes them as inner monologues; more precise structural sources and the available prose show third-person grammar.

search_log: Searched "Judy Blume Summer Sisters excerpt first chapter official" and opened the authorized prologue on Judy Blume's site and the permissioned BookBrowse reproduction.
Searched "Summer Sisters Judy Blume point of view third person narrator" and opened the BookRags whole-book point-of-view analysis.
Searched "Summer Sisters first person perspectives" and "Summer Sisters third-person narrator" to investigate whether the secondary-character sections change grammatical person.
Opened SuperSummary's character analysis, which explicitly identifies an omniscient third-person narrator that cuts among characters.
Opened an interior-passage review at Cannonball Read; its quoted secondary-character passage remains in third person.

The Harvard Crimson's ambiguous phrase "first person perspectives" prompted follow-up searches; explicit grammatical descriptions and available prose indicate it refers loosely to access to characters' perspectives, not sustained first-person narration.
Google Books and Open Library/Internet Archive previews were checked, but their searchable previews did not expose a usable sustained authorized interior excerpt.
person_note: The base narration is third person, primarily close to Vix but with brief shifts into other characters' perspectives. The diagnostic Goodreads passages q00104, q00106, and q00107 agree with the authorized third-person prologue and whole-book structural descriptions. Dialogue, maxims, and generic you statements do not alter the narrator classification. One review loosely described the inserted viewpoints as "first person perspectives," but the more precise analyses identify a third-person narrator throughout, and an available secondary-character passage also uses third-person grammar. The main remaining limitation is the absence of a sustained authorized interior excerpt, mitigated by the independent interior quotes and multiple whole-book descriptions.
